newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates slightly.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates slightly.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank on Wednesday said it had cut slightly its overnight rates in the money market.
Its overnight borrowing rate was trimmed to 9.9 percent from 10.0 percent and its overnight lending rate to 12.65 percent from 12.75 percent, the bank said.
The Central Bank had been expected to drop its overnight rates after the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rates fell to single-digit levels for two consecutive weeks.
Traders said the Central Bank had stalled such a move as it awaited the decision of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to cut interest rates in a bid to check U.S. inflation.
Late Tuesday, the U.S. FOMC raised the interest rate that commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans to 5.25 percent from 5.0 percent.

Traders said the 0.25 percentage-point hike in the U.S. interest rate was expected. Local investors had feared that a bigger increase in the U.S. rate would spawn peso speculation and forestall the moves of the Philippine Central Bank to align its rates with the market.
